exposure: Weight change category (lost, maintained, IOM recommended gain, excessive gain)
Appropriate weight gain during pregnancy (IOM recommended)
cohort: 10,734 women with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) who gave birth at 12 hospitals
finding: Compared to appropriate weight gain, weight loss during pregnancy was associated with increased risk of low birth weight but decreased risk for other maternal and neonatal morbidities, while excessive weight gain was associated with increased risk of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, macrosomia, and lower 5-minute APGAR score.
mod_finding: From weight loss to excessively gained weight, the odds of cesarean delivery increased.
